title: Google Research introduces TEE-based federated learning system
excerpt: The new system uses trusted execution environments to provide verifiable privacy guarantees for decentralized machine learning.
bodyHtml:
Google Research announced a new federated learning system on October 2, 2026, designed to provide externally verifiable privacy guarantees for machine learning models trained across decentralized data. The system utilizes Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), which are secure computing areas that allow for remote attestation, confidentiality, and integrity of data processing.

The architecture coordinates data encryption, a key management system, and workload execution to ensure that only anonymized results are released. Access policies for these workloads are published to Rekor, a public transparency log, allowing external auditors to track the server-side workloads.

Gboard has already implemented this system for its English and Japanese next-word prediction models. Google Research stated that the new infrastructure allows for faster training times by shifting computation to the server and is currently exploring its use for other workloads, including synthetic data generation.
topic: Toward provably private learning from federated data
